subject.title: resolveCliAuthEpoch invalidates every live CLI session when local credential source-of-storage flips, even though identity is unchanged

question: What should define the Claude CLI auth identity boundary for reusable sessions when an OpenClaw auth profile exists but local Claude credential storage presence changes?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the fix changes credential-boundary session reuse; automation cannot safely choose whether profile credential, host credential, or a stricter fail-closed rule owns identity without maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Identity-Stable Epoch With Fail-Closed Guardrails
options.body: Ignore local storage-source presence only when the same Claude CLI/OpenClaw auth identity is provable, and keep resetting when identity is absent, changed, or unprovable.

options.title: Profile Credential Owns The Boundary
options.body: Treat the selected OpenClaw auth profile as canonical when present and use local CLI fingerprints only for bootstrap/no-profile cases, accepting that profile identity must be sufficient for Claude CLI reuse.

options.title: Keep Storage Presence Fail-Closed
options.body: Accept the current reset behavior for ambiguous Claude CLI identity-less credentials and document the limitation rather than changing session reuse semantics now.

recommendation.title: Identity-Stable Epoch With Fail-Closed Guardrails
recommendation.body: Ignore local storage-source presence only when the same Claude CLI/OpenClaw auth identity is provable, and keep resetting when identity is absent, changed, or unprovable.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest recent history on the auth-profile/CLI epoch seams and release state, while the decision should also include security-owner review.
